lines_of_business: All lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions
sections_in_order: Description (with Summary and Analysis of Evidence)
criteria_location: Position Statement (PDF p.3) holds the main criteria; frequency cap is separate under Reimbursement Information (p.4); ICD-10 'support' list is under Billing/Coding.
procedures_covered: SI joint injection under fluoroscopy or arthrography (CPT 27096, HCPCS G0259, G0260)

logic.top_level: all (with one 'either-or' inside: two alternative conservative-therapy tracks)
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: No contraindication list. One negative rule: 'do not meet the definition of medical necessity if medical documentation indicates the injection procedures are not effective.' NSAIDs 'if not contraindicated' is an inline unless. Ultrasound guidance is declared E/I.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Phase-based: 'In the diagnostic phase, up to two (2) injections ... no sooner than one (1) week'; 'In the therapeutic phase, each subsequent injection requires that prior injection provided >= 50% pain reduction for at least six (6) weeks'. Reimbursement cap: three injections per SI joint in six months, beyond which 'subject to medical review'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Continued pain after 6 weeks with ALL of the following treatments: ... OR Worsening pain after 2 weeks with ALL of the following treatments:
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The OR sits at the same bullet level as the AND-list, and the 6-week bullet group is a sub-bullet of the top-level ALL; a parser can attach the OR to the whole policy rather than just the conservative-therapy item.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Sacroiliac joint pain for more than 3 months, AND ... Continued pain after 6 weeks
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Requires >3 months of pain but only 6 weeks (or 2 weeks) of treatment; unclear whether treatment must be within the 3 months or whether the 2-week track can ever be reached given the 3-month floor.

requirement_kinds.quote: Sacroiliac joint pain for more than 3 months
Continued pain after 6 weeks with ALL of the following: NSAIDS >= 4 weeks (if not contraindicated); Activity modification >= 6 weeks; PT, chiropractic or HEP >= 6 weeks
OR Worsening pain after 2 weeks with ALL of the following (NSAIDs, activity modification, PT/chiro/HEP)
Sacroiliac joint injections are part of a comprehensive pain treatment plan
In the therapeutic phase, each subsequent injection requires that prior injection provided >= 50% pain reduction for at least six (6) weeks
up to two (2) injections may be administered, at intervals of no sooner than one (1) week
performed under fluoroscopy or with arthrography; ultrasound investigational
ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes That Support Medical Necessity: M46.1, M47.898, M48.08, M53.2X8, M54.18, M54.30-32, M54.40-42, M54.50/51/59, M54.6, S33.2XXA/D/S, S33.6XXA/D/S
physician history and physical, radiology study reports, physician progress notes, with documentation of conservative treatment, treatment plan including narrative, and physician operative report

thresholds.quote: Sacroiliac joint pain for more than 3 months
prior injection provided ≥ 50% pain reduction for at least six (6) weeks
limited to three (3) injections per sacroiliac joint in six (6) months
up to two (2) injections may be administered

time_windows.quote: observations made six months or fewer before starting date of service

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: ICD-10 list is titled 'Codes That Support Medical Necessity' but is not mapped to any criterion; list includes M54.6 (thoracic spine pain) and S33 injury codes.
codes.non_covered_code_lists: None; ultrasound-guided injection called E/I in text but no separate code list.

external_dependencies.quote: members or providers may request a step therapy protocol exemption to this requirement if based on medical necessity

external_dependencies.what: FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines
external_dependencies.quote: Federal Employee Program (FEP): Follow FEP guidelines.

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: a diagnostic study of the joint structures. X-ray contrast is injected

vague_terms.quote: part of a comprehensive pain treatment plan

vague_terms.problem: no definition of what counts or how documented

vague_terms.quote: medical documentation indicates the injection procedures are not effective
vague_terms.problem: no threshold; overlaps with the 50%/6-week rule

extraction_hazards: Criteria bullets use o markers and indentation with an OR at same level as an AND list (pdftotext flattens)
Cap of 3 per 6 months sits in Reimbursement section, not Position Statement
Long Description section is evidence review with study numbers that look like thresholds
LOINC table is multi-column and repeats the same six-month sentence ten times
Navigation bar (Position Statement / Billing...) text appears at top of page 1
ICD-10 codes wrap onto two lines (M54.50, M54.51, / M54.59)
interesting_structures: Two alternative conservative-therapy tracks (6 weeks vs worsening pain at 2 weeks) as an OR inside an ALL
Diagnostic vs therapeutic phase with different rules
Frequency cap in reimbursement section creates a soft limit ('subject to medical review') rather than a denial
LOINC codes map required documents to time frames

fit_to_tree.why: Mostly ALL with one OR, and quantitative leaves. Strain: phase/count rules (injection history), the cap outside the criteria, and the 3-month vs 2-week tension.
